subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent dry-run across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, direct tool invocation, built-in/plugin/client tools, and before/after hooks?
rationale: The request creates a security-relevant user promise, and the current source shows multiple execution surfaces that a narrow process-global adapter flag would not cover safely.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with coverage for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

options.title: Fold into workflow modes
options.body: Keep this open but block implementation until the broader Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode defines the shared preview vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Keep only scoped dry-runs
options.body: Reject a global mode if maintainers decide it is too easy to confuse with sandboxing, and continue improving command-specific preview paths instead.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with coverage for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across the central agent runtime, shared tool adapter, Gateway direct tool surface, and CLI registration paths involved in the decision.
